author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Pete Burak discusses lessons from youth wrestling and spiritual growth
text:
Pete Burak, vice president of Renewal Ministries and a parishioner at Christ the King parish in Ann Arbor, wrote on Apr. 15 about his family’s experience with youth wrestling and its impact on personal and spiritual development. Burak shared how his seven-year-old son Zeke joined the local Irish Wrestling Club, describing the experience as transformative for both father and son.
Burak said that watching his son compete taught valuable lessons about resilience, community, and faith. He recounted a moment when Zeke lost a match but received encouragement from his coach: “One of his coaches gently held his shoulders, looked him directly in the eyes and started teaching him. Instruction morphed into encouragement, and I watched this grown man lovingly lead my young son.” Burak emphasized that these moments of loss can foster growth when experienced within an intentional community.
Reflecting on broader themes of risk-taking in faith, Burak wrote: “It’s vitally important we foster environments where we intentionally risk something for a greater cause.” He drew parallels between experiences on the wrestling mat and challenges faced in spiritual life: “In the spiritual life, we will have moments of fruitfulness and growth, and times when we fall, sin and get ‘pinned’ by temptations and corrupt desires. But if we turn to the Lord through repentance…we can keep running the race to heaven.”
Burak encouraged readers to seek out supportive communities committed to living boldly for their beliefs: “So go find your ‘wrestling club’ – other men and women who want to obey the Lord…and are willing to risk something for the sake of the Gospel.” He concluded by stating: “We cannot grow into mature disciples of Jesus Christ if we always play it safe, stay on the sidelines and don’t learn from success or defeat.”

The article highlights how experiences outside traditional religious settings can provide opportunities for personal growth within a faith context.
